verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              श्रुत्वा तु रथनिर्घोषं सिंहनादं च संयुगे । अर्जुनः प्राह गोविन्दं शीघ्रं नोदय वाजिनः ॥१॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said Hearing the loud rattles of chariots and the lion like roars (of warriors) in the field, Arjuna, addressing Govinda, said, “Clap spurs to the chargers."

verses.sanskrit: अर्जुनस्य वचः श्रुत्वा गोविंदोऽर्जुनमब्रवीत् । एष गच्छामि सुक्षिप्रं यत्र भीमो व्यवस्थितः ॥२॥
verses.english: Hearing these words of Arjuna, Govinda replied him (thus)-"Off I go towards the spot where Bhima has taken his post.”

verses.sanskrit: तं यान्तमश्वैर्हिमशङ्खवर्णैः सुवर्णमुक्तामणिजालनद्धैः । जम्भं जिघांसुं प्रगृहीतवज्रं जयाय देवेन्द्रमिवोग्रमन्युम् ॥३॥
verses.english: Then, like the king of the celestials, proceeding in great wrath and with thunder in his arms, to strike down Jambha (the Asura), Jaya (Arjuna) rushed (in the field), to obtain victory, borne by horses white as snow or conchs and with housings laid with gold, pearls and gems.

verses.sanskrit: रथाश्वमातङ्गपदातिसंघा बाणस्वनैर्नेमिखुरस्वनैश्च । संनादयन्तो वसुधां दिशश्च क्रुद्धा नृसिंहा जयमभ्युदीयुः ॥४॥
verses.english: Many warriors, (of the other side), representing lions in prowess all boiling with rage and followed by a large retinue him and making the Earth resound and rending the skies with the whizz of their arrows, the rattling sound of the wheels of their war-chariots and the noise of the tread of their horses' hoofs.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां च पार्थस्य च मारिषासीद्देहासुपापक्षपणं सुयुद्धम् । त्रैलोक्यहेतोरसुरैर्यथासीद्देवस्य विष्णोर्जयतां वरस्य ॥५॥
verses.english: Then, there ensued, O sire, a mortal conflict between them (the train-bands of the Kaurava forces) and Partha, a conflict carrying death and destruction in its train to body, life and sin alike, like the great battle between the Asuras and Vishnu, the greatest of all great conquerors, for the (sovereignty of the) three worlds.

verses.sanskrit: तैरस्तमुच्चावचमायुधं तदेकः प्रचिच्छेद किरीटमाली । क्षुरार्धचन्द्रैर्निशितैश्च भल्लैः शिरांसि तेषां बहुधा च बाहून् ॥६॥
verses.english: Alone and unaided, the diadem-decked and garland-necked Arjuna, rent asunder all the powerful weapons flung (against him) by them (his adversaries) and struck off their heads and arms in many and varied forms, with his razoredged and crescent shaped shafts, as also with his broad-pointed arrows.

verses.sanskrit: छत्राणि वालव्यजनानि केतूनश्वान्रथान्पत्तिगणान्द्विपांश्च । ते पेतुरुर्व्यां बहुधा विरूपा वातप्रणुन्नानि यथा वनानि ॥७॥
verses.english: Umbrellas, banners, horses, chariots, elephants and foot soldiers, shattered and mutilated, fell down on the Earth, like a forest uprooted by a violent wind.

verses.sanskrit: सुवर्णजालावतता महागजाः सवैजयन्तीध्वजयोधकल्पिताः । सुवर्णपुङ्खैरिषुभिः समाचिताश्चकाशिरे प्रज्वलिता यथाऽचलाः ॥८॥
verses.english: Mighty elephants caparisoned with goldlaid trappings and equipped with banners of triumphs and adorned with riders (on their back), wore a majestic look and shed a lustur all round as they were encompassed with goldwinged shafts, like blazing mountains.

verses.sanskrit: विदार्य नागाश्वरथान् धनञ्जयः शरोत्तमैर्वासववज्रसन्निभैः । द्रुतं ययौ कर्णजिघांसया तथा यथा मरुत्वान् बलभेदने पुरा ॥९॥
verses.english: With excellent shafts piercing elephants, horses and war chariots and resembling thunder of Vasava, Dhananjaya winged his way to strike down Karna, like Indra, in days of yore, proceeding to rend in twain (the Asura) Bala.

verses.sanskrit: ततः स पुरुषव्याघ्रस्तव सैन्यमरिंदमः । प्रविवेश महाबाहुर्मकरः सागरं यथा ॥१०॥
verses.english: Then that mightiest of men, the terror of enemies, rushed headlong into the midst of your vast array as does the Makar while plunging into the deep sea.

verses.sanskrit: तं हृष्टास्तावका राजन्रथपत्तिसमन्विताः । गजाश्वसादिबहुलाः पाण्डवं समुपाद्रवन् ॥११॥
verses.english: Seeing Pandu's sun so advance, O king, your warriors, with a long line of cars and a retinue of elephant, horse and foot soldiers, pressed upon him.

verses.sanskrit: तेषामापततां पार्थमारावः सुमहानभूत् । सागरस्येव क्षुब्धस्य यथा स्यात्सलिलस्वनः ॥१२॥
verses.english: And while rushing against Partha, they raised a tumultuous cry like the roarings of the surging waves in a tempest.

verses.sanskrit: ते तु तं पुरुषव्याघ्रं व्याघ्रा इव महारथाः । अभ्यद्रवन्त संग्रामे त्यक्त्वा प्राणकृतं भयम् ॥१३॥
verses.english: Those great warriors, powerful like tigers, reckless of their life, rushed in battle to face that mighty man, careering like a tiger.

verses.sanskrit: तेषामापततां तत्र शरवर्षाणि मुञ्चताम् । अर्जुनो व्यधमत्सैन्यं महावातो घनानिव ॥१४॥
verses.english: With a heavy down-pour of arrows they advanced towards him, but Arjuna dispersed them like vapours before the gushing wind.

verses.sanskrit: तेऽर्जुनं सहिता भूत्वा रथवंशैः प्रहारिणः । अभियाय महेष्वासा विव्यधुर्निशितैः शरैः ॥१५॥
verses.english: Those mighty warriors-all good shots and of unfailing aim-in a body and with a long line of war-chariots following them, advanced against Arjuna and began to pierce him with their sharp weapons.

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽर्जुनः सहस्राणि रथवारणवाजिनाम् । प्रेषयामास विशिखैर्यमस्य सदनं प्रति ॥१६॥
verses.english: Arjuna, then, (rendering asunder) with his arrows, chariots, elephants and horses by thousands, dispatched (them) off to the region of Pluto.

verses.sanskrit: ते वध्यमानाः समरे पार्थचापच्युतैः शरैः । तत्र तत्र स्म लीयन्ते भये जाते महारथाः ॥१७॥
verses.english: Thus afflicted in action with shots flung from Arjuna's bow, those mighty car-warriors, terrified and panic-stricken, began gradually to melt away.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां चतुःशतान्वीरान्यतमानान्महारथान् । अर्जुनो निशितैर्बाणैरनयद्यमसादनम् ॥१८॥
verses.english: Among those great car-warriors four hundred valiantly kept the field; and Arjuna, with his keen shafts, sent them, one and all, to their last account.

verses.sanskrit: ते वध्यमानाः समरे नानालिङ्गैः शितैः शरैः । अर्जुनं समभित्यज्य दुद्रुवुर्वै दिशो दश ॥१९॥
verses.english: (And those that held the rear) afflicted, in that battle, with keen shafts and sharp arrows of all kinds, dispersed themselves in all directions-far away from Arjuna.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां शब्दो महानासीद्द्रवतां वाहिनीमुखे । महौघस्येव जलधेर्गिरिमासाद्य दीर्यतः ॥२०॥
verses.english: The shouting noise made at the van by the retreating army was as furious as the grumbling roars of the breakers of the surging seas when dashing against rocks.

verses.sanskrit: तां तु सेनां भृशं विद्ध्वा द्रावयित्वाऽर्जुनः शरैः । प्रायादभिमुखः पार्थः सूतानीकं हि मारिष ॥२१॥
verses.english: Thus, with his arrows, dispersing the panicstricken army, O sire, Arjuna, the son of Pritha, advanced against the column commanded by the son of Suta.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य शब्दो महानासीत्परानभिमुखस्य वै। गरुडस्येव पततः पन्नगार्थे यथा पुरा ॥२२॥
verses.english: The great noise made by Arjuna while advancing towards his enemies, was like that of Garuda, in days of yore, while swooping down upon snakes.

verses.sanskrit: तं तु शब्दमभिश्रुत्य भीमसेनो महाबलः । बभूव परमप्रीतः पार्थदर्शनलालसः ॥२३॥
verses.english: The mighty Bhimasena, anxious as he was to have a look of Partha, became highly gratified with that sound.

verses.sanskrit: श्रुत्वैव पार्थमायान्तं भीमसेनः प्रतापवान् । त्यक्त्वा प्राणान्महाराज सेनां तव ममर्द ह ॥२४॥
verses.english: Hearing that Partha is come, the redoubtable Bhimasena, O king, began to afflict your troops, fearless of his own life.

verses.sanskrit: स वायुवीर्यप्रतिमो वायुवेगसमो जवे । वायुवद्व्यचरद्भीमो वायुपुत्रः प्रतापवान् ॥२५॥
verses.english: Bhima, the son of the Wind-god and himself possessing the prowess and impetuousity of the wind, that valiant Bhima began to career in that battle like that of the wind itself.

verses.sanskrit: तेनार्द्यमाना राजेन्द्र सेना तव विशांपते । व्यभ्रश्यत महाराज भिन्ना नौरिव सागरे ॥२६॥
verses.english: Your army, O king, being thus hard pressed by him, O ruler of the universe, began to roll and tumble like a shattered vessel in the high seas.

verses.sanskrit: तां तु सेनां तदा भीमो दर्शयन् पाणिलाघवम् । शरैरवचकर्तोग्रैः प्रेषयिष्यन् यमक्षयम् ॥२७॥
verses.english: Bhima then, with his deadly weapons and with great dexterity of hands, waging a ruthless slaughter amongst that body of troops, dispatched them to the region of Pluto.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र भारत भीमस्य बलं दृष्ट्वाऽतिमानुषम् । व्यभ्रमन्त रणे योधाः कालस्येव युगक्षये ॥२८॥
verses.english: Your warriors, O Bharata, seeing the wonderful exploits of Bhima in that battle, careering like the King of Terrors at the end of time, became greatly agitated.

verses.sanskrit: तथाऽर्दितान्भीमबलान् भीमसेनेन भारत । दृष्ट्वा दुर्योधनो राजा इदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥२९॥
verses.english: King Duryodhana, seeing his best soldiers, O Bharata, thus worsted by Bhimasena, gave vent to the following expression, addressing his whole hosts, generals and other great warriors, O best of the Bharata race, "All of you in a body engaged Bhima in action and fell him down (inasmuch as on him hinges the fate of the Pandavas).

verses.sanskrit: सैनिकांश्च महेष्वासान् योधांश्च भरतर्षभ । समादिशन्रणे सर्वान्हत भीममिति स्म ह ॥३०॥
तस्मिन्हते हतं मन्ये पाण्डुसैन्यमशेषतः । प्रतिगृह्य च तामाज्ञां तव पुत्रस्य पार्थिवाः ॥३१॥
verses.english: When he (Bhimasena) is felled, well may I count upon the Pandu forces as if already slain. Following the behest of your son, all the vassal chiefs (hitting) from all sides, covered Bhima with a thick shower of arrows.

verses.sanskrit: भीमं प्रच्छा‌दयामासुः शरवर्षैः समन्ततः । गजाश्च बहुला राजन्नराश्च जयगृद्धिनः ॥३२॥
verses.english: Hosts of elephants, O monarch and men, eager for victory, as also war-chariots and horses, O King of Kings, thickened around Vrikodara.

verses.sanskrit: रथे स्थिताश्च राजेन्द्र परिवव्रुर्वृकोदरम् । स तैः परिवृतः शूरैः शूरो राजन्समन्ततः ॥३३॥
verses.english: That chef of the Bharata race, endued with heroic qualities, being thus hemmed in by those brave bands of heroes, looked resplendent like the radiant Moon shedding its effulgence amidst myriads of glowing stars.

verses.sanskrit: शुशुभे भरतश्रेष्ठो नक्षत्रैरिव चन्द्रमाः । परिवेषी यथा सोमः परिपूर्णो विराजते ॥३४॥
स रराज तथा संख्ये दर्शनीयो नरोत्तमः । निर्विशेषो महाराज यथा हि विजयस्तथा ॥३५॥
verses.english: O monarch, that foremost of men, was looking, during that fight, so beautiful, like the full Moon in the midst of his corona. He look like Arjuna. There is no difference between him and Arjuna.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य ते पार्थिवाः सर्वे शरवृष्टिं समासृजन् । क्रोधरक्तेक्षणाः शूरा हन्तुकामा वृकोद्रम् ॥३६॥
verses.english: All those kings with eyes flamed with wrath and bent upon slaying Vrikodara, began to shower down their weapons upon him.

verses.sanskrit: तां विदार्य महासेनां शरैः सन्नतपर्वभिः । निश्चक्राम रणाद्भीमो मत्स्योजालादिवांभसि ॥३७॥
verses.english: As the fish frees itself from the net, so did Bhima cutting their shafts straight free himself from the pressure of the battle.

verses.sanskrit: हत्वा दशसहस्राणि गजानामनिवर्तिनाम् । नृणां शतसहस्त्रे द्वे द्वे शते चैव भारत ॥३८॥
verses.english: O Bharata slaying ten thousand elephants that faced him, two lakhs two hundred men, hundred car-warriors and five thousand horses Bhima actually made a river of blood to flow there.

verses.sanskrit: पञ्च चाश्वसहस्राणि रथानां शतमेव च । हत्वा प्रास्यन्दयद्भीमो नदीं शोणितवाहिनीम् ॥३९॥
शोणितोदां रथावर्तां हस्तिग्राहसमाकुलाम् । नरमीनाश्वनक्रान्तां केशशैवलशाद्वलाम् ॥४०॥
verses.english: In that carnage blood flowed like water and the war-cars forming its eddies, elephants, its alligators, horses and men, its sharks and fishes and the hair of animals, its herbs and moss, were all floating on it. Arms severed from bodies floated like snakes and precious stones were abundant in the bloody current; thighs and marrows formed its gavials and mud and human heads, its mountain. Iron bound bludgeous and maces were also floating there like snakes, and bows and arrows formed its rafts by means of which persons tried to cross that fearful and bloody stream, banners and umbrellas drifted on it like swans and costly head-dresses its foam. The dust rising from the earth were like the waves of the stream and jeweled necklaces were looking like so many lotuses; the brave could alone cross that stream while the faint hearted sunk within to navigate it. That gushing current, with hands of sturdy soldiers forming its alligators and crocodiles, streamed its course towards the realm of Death. (and) and that man with tiger-like ferocity made its course flew on. (And) as the Vaitarani is unnavigable by persons of fifth and inequity, even so was that awful stream of blood to men wanting in valour and intrepidity, making their heart quail with shudder.

verses.sanskrit: संच्छिन्नभुजनागेन्द्रां बहुरत्नापहारिणीम् । ऊरुग्राहां मज्जपङ्कां शीर्षोपलसमावृताम् ॥४१॥
धनुःकाशां शरावापां गदापरिघकेतनाम् । हंसछत्रध्वजोपेतामुष्णीषवरफेनिलाम् ॥४२॥
हारपद्माकरां चैव भूमिरेणूर्मिमालिनीम् । आर्यवृत्तवतीं संख्ये सुतरां भीरुदुस्तराम् ॥४३॥
योधग्राहवतीं संख्ये वहन्तीं पितृसादनम् । क्षणेन पुरुषव्याघ्रः प्रावर्तयत निम्नगाम् ॥४४॥
यथा वैतरणीमुग्रां दुस्तरामकृतात्मभिः । तथा दुस्तरणीं घोरां भीरूणां भयवर्धनीम् ॥४५॥
यतो यतः पाण्डवेयः प्रविष्टो रथसत्तमः । ततस्ततो घातयत योधाञ्शतसहस्रशः ॥४६॥
verses.english: (And) there that son of Pandu, the best of car-warriors, rushed in, slaying hundred thousands of enemy.

verses.sanskrit: एवं दृष्ट्वा कृतं कर्म भीमसेनेन संयुगे । दुर्योधनो महाराज शकुनिं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥४७॥
verses.english: Duryodhana seeing Bhimasena thus career in battle, ( king said unto Shakuni the following words-

verses.sanskrit: जहि मातुल संग्रामे भीमसेनं महाबलम् । अस्मिञ्जिते जितं मन्ये पाण्डवेयं महाबलम् ॥४८॥
verses.english: Overpower in the battle, O uncle, the allpowerful Bhimasena. The victory over the vast array of the Pandava forces hinges on his final overthrow.

verses.sanskrit: ततः प्रायान्महाराज सौबलेयः प्रतापवान् । रणाय महते युक्तो भ्रातृभिः परिवारितः ॥४९॥
verses.english: Being thus desired, O king, the powerful son of Subala, the peer of great warriors marshaled in array, marched on-his brothers surrounding him. That hero, affronting the fiercely powerful Bhima in that battle, checked his intrepidity, as if a continent resisting the tides of an ocean.

verses.sanskrit: स समासाद्य संग्रामे भीमं भीमपराक्रमम् । वारयामास तं वीरो वेलेव मकरालयम् ॥५०॥
संन्यवर्तत तं भीमो वार्यमाणः शितैः शरैः । शकुनिस्तस्य राजेन्द्र वामपार्श्वे स्तनान्तरे ॥५१॥
verses.english: And despite he resistance of the keen shafts, (which the powerful son of Subala hurled against him,) Bhima approached him (in formidable array). Whereupon Shakuni, O king of kings, flung a number of cloth-yard shafts, bedecked with wings of gold and sharpened on stone and assailed Bhima at the seat of his heart.

verses.sanskrit: प्रेषयामास नाराचान् रुक्मपुङ्खाञ्शिलाशितान् । वर्म भित्त्वा तु ते घोराः पाण्डवस्य महात्मनः ॥५२॥
न्यमज्जन्त महाराज कङ्कबर्हिणवाससः । सोऽतिविद्धो रणे भीमः शरं रुक्मविभूषितम् ॥५३॥
verses.english: Those fearful shafts, feathered with the plumes of Kankas and peacocks, O monarch, piercing the coat of mail of the high-souled son of Pandu, sunk deep into his vital parts.

verses.sanskrit: प्रेषयामास स रुषा सौबलं प्रति भारत । तमायान्तं शरं घोरं शकुनिः शत्रुतापनः ॥५४॥
verses.english: Being thus smitten in battle, O Bharata, Bhima, then flung, all of a sudden, a shaft laid with gold upon the son of Subala.

verses.sanskrit: चिच्छेद सप्तधा राजन् कृतहस्तो महाबलः । तस्मिन्निपतिते भूमौ भीमः क्रुद्धो विशांपते ॥५५॥
verses.english: And the powerful Shakuni, the inflictor of woes on his enemies and O king, skillful in the manipulation of hands, rent that fearful weapon in seven fragments as it was coursing its way towards him.

verses.sanskrit: धनुश्छिच्छेद भल्लेन सौबलस्य हसन्निव । तदपास्य धनुश्छिन्नं सौबलेयः प्रतापवान् ॥५६॥
verses.english: Whereupon the mighty son of Subala, throwing away that bow, rendered useless, with the greatest alacrity seized a new one, as also sixteen broad-edged shafts.

verses.sanskrit: अन्यदादाय वेगेन धनुर्भल्लांश्च षोडश । तैस्तस्य तु महाराज भल्लैः सन्नतपर्वभिः ॥५७॥
verses.english: And the son of Subala, O king, hit the chariot-driver with two and Bhima with seven; struck off the banner with one and the umbrella with two; and pierced, O lord of the universe, the four chargers with the remaining four chargers with the remaining four of those broad-headed shafts.

verses.sanskrit: द्वाभ्यां स सारथिं ह्यार्च्छद्भीमं सप्तभिरेव च । ध्वजमेकेन चिच्छेद द्वाभ्यां छत्रं विशांपते ॥५८॥
चतुर्भिश्चतुरो वाहान्विव्याध सुबलात्मजः । ततः क्रुद्धो महाराज भीमसेनः प्रतापवान् ॥५९॥
शक्तिं चिक्षेप समरे रुक्मदण्डामयस्मयीम् । सा भीमभुजनिर्मुक्ता नागजिह्वेव चञ्चला ॥६०॥
verses.english: Enraged at this, O king, the powerful Bhima, in that battle, threw down a weapon made of iron and the staff of which was decked with gold.

verses.sanskrit: निपपात रणे तूर्णं सौबलस्य महात्मनः । ततस्तामेव संगृह्य शक्तिं कनकभूषणाम् ॥६१॥
verses.english: That weapon, resembling in activity the tongue of a snake, being thus cast from the arms of Bhima came speedily down upon the chariot of the noble son of Subala.

verses.sanskrit: भीमसेनाय चिक्षेप क्रुद्धरूपो विशांपते । सा निर्भिद्य भुजं सव्यं पाण्डवस्य महात्मनः ॥६२॥
verses.english: (And) he (the son of Subala) seized that weapon, adorned with gold and O lord of the universe, hurled it back against Bhimasena with a fierce countenance,

verses.sanskrit: निपपात तदा भूमौ यथा विद्युन्नभश्च्युता । अथोत्क्रुष्टं महाराज धार्तराष्ट्रैः समन्ततः ॥६३॥
verses.english: That weapon, piercing through the left arm of the noble son of Pandu, fell down like flashes of lightning coursing on the ground.

verses.sanskrit: न तु तं ममृषे भीमः सिंहनादं तरस्विनाम् । अन्यद्गृह्य धनुः सज्यं त्वरमाणो महाबलः ॥६४॥
verses.english: Then the Dhartarashtras began to rent the air from all sides with their loud out-crics, but, O king, Bhima could not brook the lion-like roars of the enemy, all of great intrepidity.

verses.sanskrit: मुहूर्तादिव राजेन्द्र च्छादयामास सायकैः । सौबलस्य बलं संख्ये त्यक्त्वाऽऽमानं महाबलः ॥६५॥
verses.english: That extraordinarily powerful man (Bhima) taking hold of another bow fitted with string, almost in no time, O best of kings, covered the mighty son of Subala and his forces, who were fighting valiantly without caring the least for their lives, with showers of arrows.

verses.sanskrit: तस्याश्वांश्चतुरो हत्वा सूतं चैव विशांपते । ध्वजं चिच्छेद भल्लेन त्वरमाणः पराक्रमी ॥६६॥
verses.english: That mighty man (Bhimasena) with utmost intrepidity stricking off his (Shakuni's) four horses and then sending his charioteer to his eternal rest, O ruler of the universe, rent asunder his adversary's banner with a broadedged arrow.

verses.sanskrit: हताश्वं रथमुत्सृज्य त्वरमाणो नरोत्तमः । तस्थौ विस्फारयंश्चापं क्रोधरक्तेक्षणः श्वसन् ॥६७॥
verses.english: Speedily bounding out of that steedless chariot, Shakuni, the best of men, with eyes flaming with wrath and stretched bow, took his stand on the ground, breathing all the while heavy breaths.

verses.sanskrit: शरैश्च बहुधा राजन् भीममार्च्छत्समन्ततः । प्रतिहत्य तु वेगेन भमिसेनः प्रतापवान् ॥६८॥
verses.english: And then, O king, he covered Bhima with numberless arrows from all sides. Then the mighty Bhima rending asunder Shakuni's arrows with great wrath hit him with a host of sharp arrows.

verses.sanskrit: धनुश्चिच्छेद संक्रुद्धो विव्याध च शितैः शरैः । सोऽतिविद्धो बलवता शत्रुणा शत्रुकर्शनः ॥६९॥
निपपात तदा भूमौ किञ्चित्प्राणो नराधिपः । ततस्तं विह्वलं ज्ञात्वा पुत्रस्तव विशांपते ॥७०॥
verses.english: Being thus afflicted by his powerful assailant, that destroyer of enemies, O king, dropped down on the Earth almost dead.

verses.sanskrit: अपोवाह रथेनाजौ भीमसेनस्य पश्यतः । रथस्थे तु नरव्याघ्रे धार्तराष्ट्राः पराङ्मुखाः ॥७१॥
verses.english: Seeing him (Shakuni) in such a woeful plight, your son, O supreme ruler of the universe, putting him in his own chariot carried him off from the scene of action before the very face of Bhimasena.

verses.sanskrit: प्रदुद्रुवुर्दिशो भीता भीमाज्जाते महाभये । सौबले निर्जिते राजन्भीमसेनेन धन्विना ॥७२॥
verses.english: Seeing that foremost of men, Shakuni, thus knocked down and borne away on Duryodhana's chariot, the Imperial hosts began to beat a hasty retreat from the field and flew in all directions from the very fear of Bhimasena.

verses.sanskrit: भयेन महताऽऽविष्टः पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव । अपायाज्जवनैरश्वैः सापेक्षो मातुलं प्रति ॥७३॥
verses.english: When the son of Subala was thus discomfited and defeated, O monarch, by that excellent archer (Bhimasena) your son Duryodhana, left the field in a state of trepidation and out of his concern for the life of his uncle Shakuni, urged his fiery chargers to a furious speed.

verses.sanskrit: पराङ्मुखं तु राजानं दृष्ट्वा सैन्यानि भारत । विप्रजग्मुः समुत्सृज्य द्वैरथानि समन्ततः ॥७४॥
verses.english: Seeing the king thus flee away from the battle, all his troops, O foremost of the line of Bharata, who were each engaged in fierce struggle with a hand-to-hand fight, began to disperse themselves in all directions.

verses.sanskrit: तान् दृष्ट्वा विद्रुतान्सर्वान् धार्तराष्ट्रान्पराङ्मुखान् । जवेनाभ्यापतद्भीमः किरञ्शरशतान्बहून् ॥७५॥
verses.english: Observing the whole hosts of the Dhritarasthra force thus dispersing themselves in every direction, Bhima, with great impetuosity rushed against them and attacked them with innumerable arrows.

verses.sanskrit: ते वध्यमाना भीमेन धार्तराष्ट्राः पराङ्मुखाः । कर्णमासाद्य समरे स्थिता राजन् समन्ततः ॥७६॥
verses.english: Thus afflicted by Bhima, O monarch, the retreating bands of Dhritarashtra's army (all in a body moved towards Karna's flank).

verses.sanskrit: स हि तेषां महावीर्यो द्वीपोऽभूत्सुमहाबलः । भिन्ननौका यथा राजन्द्वीपमासाद्य निर्वृताः ॥७७॥
verses.english: And coming thither and with them (General Karna) in their centre, they once more held there ground. As the ship-wrecked mariners become comforted in reaching in island, so your distressed army stood cheerfully on finding that mighty Karna. O foremost of the Bharata race, O inightiest of men, O lord of the universe, they then proceeded having death for their ultimate end.

verses.sanskrit: भवन्ति पुरुषव्याघ्र नाविकाः कालपर्यये । तथा कर्णं समासाद्य तावकाः पुरुषर्षभ ॥७८॥
समाश्वस्ताः स्थिता राजन्संप्रहृष्टाः परस्परम् । समाजग्मुश्च युद्धाय मृत्युं कृत्वा निवर्तनम् ॥७९॥
